newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end weak day sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end weak day sharply lower.

text.p: Swiss shares ended a weak day sharply lower on moderate volumes after Wall Street opening losses led to a late slide on the Swiss bourse, dealers said.
Dealers were disappointed with the market's fall below 3,700 SMI points.
"Presently, Zurich only follows negative moves on Wall Street, not the positive ones", a dealer said.
Trade was dominated by professional and prices are expected to remain volatile throughout the week.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 32.7 points, or 0.88 percent, to 3,690.0 points and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 17.22 points, or 0.72 percent, to 2,366.78 points.
Derivatives-linked transactions put several blue chips under heavy pressure. But the losses were mostly a reaction to recent gains, a dealers said.
Elektrowatt was the only winner among blue chips, adding four francs to 498 on speculative buying.
Financials were clearly lower. CS Holding, UBS and major insurers Winterthur, Zurich and Swiss Re shed more than one percent each.
Pharmaceutical Roche fell 100 francs, or 1.07 percent, to 9,260. Ciba and Sandoz were also lower.
Nestle continued its recent downward move, triggered by last Friday's restrained outlook for the second half of 1996. The shares lost nine francs to 1,389 francs.
High-tech group Esec shot up 425 francs to 5,050. Dealers said the shares shook off a recent weak tendendy, profiting from the company's confident sales outlook.
Ascom, which reported that first half operating profit rose 39 percent, fell 20 francs to 1,285.
